bill.title: Combating Organized Retail Crime Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The bill directly addresses organized theft targeting retail operations and e-commerce platforms.
The bill explicitly covers theft from interstate and foreign shipments, affecting logistics and shipping companies.
The bill addresses online marketplaces and social media platforms where stolen goods are sold, potentially creating new compliance obligations.
The bill expands money laundering statutes to cover prepaid cards and gift cards, affecting payment processors and card issuers.

bill.plainSummary: This bill expands federal authority to prosecute organized retail theft and supply-chain crime. It allows prosecutors to aggregate the value of stolen goods over a 12-month period to meet felony thresholds, makes these offenses predicate crimes for money laundering charges, and authorizes asset forfeiture. The bill also creates a temporary coordination center within the Department of Homeland Security to help federal agencies work together on these cases.

bill.title: CARE Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance. (Sponsor introductory remarks on measure: CR S7964)

industries.rationale: The bill creates a new Medicare payment stream for ground ambulance services that do not result in transport, directly affecting ambulance operators' revenues and service models.
Medicare payment policy changes for emergency medical services affect the program's costs and may influence private insurers' coverage decisions for similar services.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs Medicare to test a five-year program that would pay ambulance services even when they respond to an emergency call but do not transport the patient to a hospital. Payment rates would generally match what Medicare currently pays when a patient is transported. The Government Accountability Office would study how the program affects Medicare beneficiaries' access to emergency medical services and their health outcomes.

bill.title: Removing Medicare Mental Health Inpatient Limitations Act of 2026
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.

industries.rationale: Psychiatric hospitals and mental health facilities would see expanded Medicare reimbursement eligibility for inpatient services beyond the current 190-day cap.
Medicare program costs would increase as the lifetime limit is removed, affecting federal health insurance expenditures and potentially Medicare Advantage plan costs.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would eliminate the current 190-day lifetime cap on inpatient psychiatric hospital care covered by Medicare. Under current law, Medicare beneficiaries can receive only 190 days of inpatient psychiatric hospital services over their entire lifetime; this bill would remove that limit. The change would allow Medicare beneficiaries with serious mental health conditions to access inpatient psychiatric care beyond the current lifetime maximum.

bill.title: ABC Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.

industries.rationale: Streamlined administrative processes for Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP may affect how providers interact with patients' caregivers and handle eligibility documentation.
Changes to Medicare and Medicaid administrative processes could affect insurers participating in these programs and their coordination with caregivers.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs federal agencies to review and simplify the paperwork and application processes for Medicare, Medicaid, the Children's Health Insurance Program, and Social Security. The goal is to reduce the burden on family caregivers by eliminating duplicative forms and streamlining eligibility procedures across these programs. Agencies must gather input from caregivers and state organizations, make improvements, and report their progress to Congress.

bill.title: National Plan for Epilepsy Act
bill.latestActionText: Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.

industries.rationale: The bill's focus on epilepsy treatment, diagnosis, and cure research directly affects pharmaceutical and medical device companies developing epilepsy therapies.
The national plan's coordination of epilepsy care and services would affect hospitals and health systems that diagnose and treat epilepsy patients.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services to create and carry out a national plan to address epilepsy, including prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and research coordination across federal agencies. HHS must establish an advisory council that reports to Congress every two years and must itself submit annual progress reports with recommended actions. These requirements would remain in effect until the end of 2035.

bill.title: Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 461.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services

industries.rationale: The bill directly funds research and development of drugs and therapies for ALS and neurodegenerative diseases, affecting pharmaceutical and biotech companies developing these treatments.
Clinical trial enrollment requirements and expanded access to investigational drugs may affect hospitals and health systems conducting ALS research and treatment.

bill.plainSummary: This bill extends funding through fiscal year 2031 for federal programs that support research and development of treatments for ALS (Lou Gehrig's disease) and similar neurodegenerative diseases. It requires the National Institutes of Health to track safety data more closely when awarding grants for experimental drug studies, and directs the Food and Drug Administration to publish five-year plans describing how it will help develop and approve treatments for these rare diseases. The bill also mandates reports evaluating the effectiveness of these grant programs.

bill.title: HALT Fentanyl Act

industries.rationale: The bill changes registration and licensing requirements for pharmaceutical researchers conducting controlled substance research and affects the regulatory classification of chemical substances.
The bill establishes new criminal penalties and quantity thresholds that will affect prosecution and defense of drug trafficking cases.
Universities and research institutions conducting controlled substance research would be subject to the new registration processes and requirements established by the bill.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would permanently classify all fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I controlled substances, meaning they would be treated as having high abuse potential and no accepted medical use. It sets the same criminal penalties and quantity thresholds for fentanyl-related substances as currently apply to fentanyl analogues. The bill also creates a streamlined registration process for researchers studying Schedule I substances and relaxes some requirements for research facilities working with controlled substances.

bill.title: Laken Riley Act

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new detention mandates on DHS and creates liability exposure for federal agencies, while authorizing state governments to bring suit over immigration enforcement.

The bill creates new grounds for state litigation against the federal government and expands detention requirements, generating demand for legal services in immigration and intergovernmental litigation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security to detain certain non-citizens who are in the country unlawfully and have been arrested for or charged with crimes including burglary, theft, assault on law enforcement, or offenses causing death or serious injury. It also allows state governments to sue the federal government if immigration enforcement decisions or failures—such as releasing detainees, not conducting required asylum interviews, or violating parole limitations—cause harm to the state or its residents, including financial harm exceeding $100.

bill.title: A joint resolution terminating the national emergency declared to impose duties on articles imported from Canada.
subjects: Presidents and presidential powers, Vice Presidents

industries.rationale: The resolution directly affects the 10% tariff on Canadian energy and energy resources.
The 25% tariff on most Canadian imports affects manufacturers who source materials, components, or finished goods from Canada.
Retailers importing consumer goods from Canada face the 25% tariff that this resolution would eliminate.
Agricultural products and food imports from Canada are subject to the 25% tariff.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution would end the national emergency that President Trump declared on February 1, 2025, which imposed a 25% tariff on most goods imported from Canada and a 10% tariff on Canadian energy imports. Terminating the emergency would remove the legal basis for these additional duties on Canadian products.

bill.title: Whole Milk for Healthy Kids Act of 2025

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects dairy producers and processors by expanding the types of milk schools may purchase and serve.
Schools participating in the lunch program face new training requirements and changes to meal planning and procurement rules.
Food service companies and suppliers to school meal programs would adjust product offerings to meet the expanded milk and nondairy beverage options.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would allow schools participating in the National School Lunch Program to offer whole milk and 2% milk to students, in addition to the low-fat and fat-free options currently required. It would expand nondairy milk alternatives, permit parents (not just doctors) to request milk substitutes for students with dietary restrictions, and exclude milk fat from saturated fat limits in school meals. The bill also requires annual food allergy training and certification for school food service staff.

plain.whoItTouches: Parents of young children. People who use food aid.
